steps.name: Load, reconcile, and QC counts/metadata
caveats: The counts file has 7 sample columns against a 6-row metadata table (3 treated vs 3 control) — do not assume they align positionally; match on sample ID and report explicitly if one counts column has no metadata match or must be dropped

Do not filter genes so aggressively that low-count genes relevant to a small liver panel are lost prematurely — use a standard low-count filter (e.g., min count sum or CPM threshold) documented explicitly
steps.question: Do the raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes) and the sample metadata (condition: treated vs control) align, and what do library size, gene detection, and count distributions look like across the 3 treated vs 3 control samples?
acceptance_criteria: Counts and metadata sample identifiers are matched and reconciled; any discrepancy between the 7 count columns and the 6 metadata rows is explicitly resolved and reported (e.g., extra column dropped or identified as duplicate/mislabel) with justification, not silently ignored
Final analysis-ready count matrix and metadata confirm exactly 3 treated and 3 control samples, unpaired, single batch
Library size, total detected genes per sample, and a sample-sample correlation/PCA are reported to flag any outlier sample before DE testing

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
caveats: n=3 per group gives a minimum of 2 residual degrees of freedom per gene for dispersion estimation before pooling — DESeq2's empirical Bayes shrinkage compensates but do not claim gene-wise dispersion is well-estimated independently
Use apeglm shrinkage rather than raw MLE log2FoldChange for ranking/reporting effect sizes, since raw LFCs are noisy at this sample size
steps.question: Which genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples (Wald test, BH-adjusted p<0.05, with apeglm-shrunk log2 fold changes)?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 model fit on the reconciled raw integer counts with condition (treated vs control) as the sole design factor
Output table includes baseMean, shrunken log2FoldChange (apeglm), p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value for every gene, sorted by adjusted p-value
Number of significant DE genes at padj<0.05 and at a more conservative padj<0.01 is reported, plus a volcano plot and dispersion plot are generated

steps.name: Power and confidence assessment for n=3 vs n=3 design
caveats: With only 3 vs 3 samples, leave-one-out results are themselves noisy — report them as a stability indicator, not as validation of biological truth
Do not present any post-hoc power number as a formal a priori power calculation; frame it as a diagnostic on the observed dispersion/effect-size distribution
steps.question: Given only 3 replicates per arm, how much statistical confidence do the treated-vs-control DE calls actually carry, and how sensitive are the results to a single sample being removed or to the multiple-testing correction chosen?
acceptance_criteria: Leave-one-out re-analysis (drop each of the 6 samples in turn, rerun DESeq2) reports how many of the original significant genes remain significant, quantifying result stability under n=2-vs-3 or n=3-vs-2 perturbation
Dispersion estimate diagnostics (gene-wise vs fitted vs final/shrunk dispersion, and the dispersion plot) are interpreted specifically in terms of what n=3 replication allows and does not allow
A comparison of nominal p-value distribution (histogram) against the uniform expectation is reported to flag any miscalibration typical of very small n

A plain-language statement of achievable statistical power at this sample size (e.g., approximate power to detect a 2-fold change at typical dispersion, referencing standard RNA-seq power literature/guidance) is included, explicitly separating what padj<0.05 calls do and do not guarantee here

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of significant DE genes
caveats: WikiPathways human gene sets use HGNC gene symbols — confirm the counts file's gene identifier column is also HGNC symbol before matching, or convert if it uses a different namespace

Enrichment results from a handful of DE genes at n=3 per group should be reported as exploratory/hypothesis-generating, consistent with the limited power flagged in T1S3, not as confirmed pathway involvement
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes significantly differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis run on the padj<0.05 DE gene list from T1S2 against WikiPathways human gene sets

If fewer than ~10 significant genes are returned by T1S2, the step reports this explicitly and falls back to a ranked (fgsea-style) enrichment on the full ranked gene list rather than failing silently
Enriched pathways reported with adjusted p-values and the overlapping gene members, contextualized as liver/drug-treatment relevant where applicable

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DESeq2 DE with power caveats
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a bulk RNA-seq liver drug-treatment study with raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 7 samples in the counts file; metadata describes a 3-vs-3 design across 6 samples, unpaired, single batch — note the counts file column count (7) exceeds the metadata row count (6), which the first step must reconcile before any modeling). With only n=3 per arm, standard DESeq2 shrinkage-based testing is appropriate but statistical power is inherently limited: the pipeline must explicitly quantify and report that limitation (this is the core of the research question, not an afterthought) rather than just deliver a gene list. Step 1 loads and QC's the counts/metadata, reconciling any sample mismatch and checking library size and gene detection distributions. Step 2 runs DESeq2 (Wald test, apeglm LFC shrinkage) for the treated-vs-control contrast, producing the DE gene table. Step 3 performs a dedicated power/confidence assessment appropriate to n=3 per group: dispersion estimate stability, post-hoc power curves via effect-size/dispersion relationships, sensitivity to outlier removal (e.g., leave-one-out), and correction-method comparison (BH vs more conservative options), to give an honest answer to 'how confident can we be'. Step 4 runs pathway enrichment (WikiPathways human gene sets, confirmed present in the reference store) on the significant DE genes to add biological interpretation, contingent on the DE step yielding a usable gene list.
